description: Oesophageal new consult. Short and somewhat noisy transcript — partial sentences, self-correction. Explicit GP action (24-hour pH monitoring). Explicit pronoun (she/her). Tests: short/noisy transcript handling, pronoun adherence, oesophageal routing (NEW_LETTER not FUNCTIONAL).
transcript:
Gastroenterologist: Good morning Sandra, thanks for coming in. So tell me what's been going on.

Patient: I've had this burning — kind of, um — it's like a burning feeling in my chest, gets worse after eating, particularly acidic food. And sometimes... sometimes I wake up at night with it. It's been about six months.

Gastroenterologist: Right, so heartburn symptoms, nocturnal reflux, six months duration. She's a 44-year-old woman. No dysphagia. No weight loss. She's been taking over-the-counter antacids — doesn't know the name — with partial relief. No history of peptic ulcer disease. She takes no regular medications.

Patient: Could it be — what's it called — acid reflux?

Gastroenterologist: Yes, this is consistent with gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. I want to get a gastroscopy first — I've organised that for two weeks from now. Depending on those results, if I need better characterisation of the reflux, I may organise a 24-hour ambulatory pH monitoring. I'll ask Dr Peterson to start her on a proton pump inhibitor in the interim — omeprazole 20 milligrams once daily before breakfast.

Patient: Okay, good. Thank you.

Gastroenterologist: I'll write to Dr Peterson with a full summary.
